To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) polynomial approximation combined with table lookup is a good choice for many functions and accuracy requirements, and that (2) the design space of function evaluation methods is large and that (3) the design space exploration can be automated to a large extent.

(1) for a given accuracy, polynomial approximation is the best choice for functions with a high frequency of small inputs and table lookup is the best choice when inputs are large; (2) for a given precision and accuracy, the optimal polynomial order depends on the function; and (3) the design space of function evaluation units is very large and the optimal choice of function evaluation unit depends on a variety of factors.

(a) for a given function evaluation method, the accuracy requirement determines the precision of the coefficients, and (b) for a given accuracy, the function evaluation method determines the precision of coefficients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the automation of the function evaluation unit design.
the design space exploration of function evaluation units for FPGAs, and the automation of the design process.
the automation of the design of function evaluation for FPGAs, which is a key step in the design of many compute-intensive algorithms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our methodology and tools are capable of producing a wide variety of optimized hardware implementations for a given accuracy requirement.
the best function evaluation design is highly dependent on the accuracy requirement, the technology mapping and the optimization metrics.
our methodology provides an effective and efficient design space exploration for function evaluation units on reconfigurable hardware.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed methodology is a step towards a more automated FPGA design process, and that it provides a good starting point for the exploration of the design space of function evaluation.
the design of optimized table-with-polynomial function evaluation units can be automated and the results can be integrated in ASC, a stream compiler for FPGAs.
we can design function evaluation units for FPGAs with an average of 10x better throughput than a naive table-based implementation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the design space is large and that the optimal design depends on the accuracy, precision and the technology.
the design of a function evaluation unit for a given application is a nontrivial task.
the design space of function evaluation units is large, with many different design points.
